title: Simultaneous Galois partitions for Noetherian constructible module sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a scheme [def-pc-scheme] admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, and let $E_1,\ldots,E_m$ be sheaves of modules over $R_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. A sheaf is called constructible if there is a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on each stratum of which its inverse-image restriction is locally constant with finitely generated $R$-module values [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules, def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose every $E_j$ is constructible. There is a finite locally closed stratification $X=\coprod_i S_i$ by nonempty connected reduced subschemes [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-reduced-scheme] and, for each $i$, a connected finite etale Galois cover $c_i:V_i\to S_i$ [def-galois-object] such that for every $j$ there is a finitely presented $R$-module $M_{ij}$ and an isomorphism $c_i^{-1}(E_j|_{S_i})\cong\underline{M_{ij}}_{V_i}$. Restrictions use module inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Finitely presented means that there is an exact sequence $R^r\to R^s\to M_{ij}\to0$ for finite $r,s\ge0$. No flatness or finite underlying-set hypothesis is imposed on $E_j$ or $R$. For $X=\varnothing$ the stratification is empty; an empty family of sheaves is permitted.

source.place: Tags 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules), 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite), and 03SF (pione.tex, section-finite-etale-under-galois), applied simultaneously to a finite family of affine-free presentations; ILO XVII Definition 7.3.1 and the Galois partitions used in the proof of Theorem 7.6.1, p. 314.

proof.text: First suppose $X\ne\varnothing$ and $m>0$. Take a common refinement of the finitely many given stratifications, successively applying [lemma-constructible-common-refinement]. Replace every nonempty stratum by its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. These still give a finite locally closed partition. A reduced refined stratum maps to each original stratum: restrict to the open in a closed-then-open factorization of that immersion, then use [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] for its closed part. This justifies actual morphisms to the old strata, rather than merely set-theoretic containment. Denote the resulting reduced strata by $T$.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite), common-refinement operation; reduced strata as in ILO XVII Definition 7.3.1

proof.text: Every such $T$ is Noetherian and qcqs. Here are the elementary Noetherian checks: locally a locally closed subscheme has charts obtained by first restricting an affine Noetherian chart and then quotienting its ring; every ideal of a localization is generated by the images of generators of its contraction, and every ideal of a quotient is generated by the images of generators of its inverse image. Thus these rings are Noetherian. The underlying space of $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], and every subset is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets]; hence $T$ is quasi-compact and its affine cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separatedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. The same argument applies to every later locally closed refinement and reduction. Topological Noetherianity passes to a subspace: lift an increasing chain of relative opens to ambient opens and take successive unions, so stabilization of the latter stabilizes the former.

Fix $T$. For each $j$, pull the local constant descriptions on the old stratum back to $T$. They remain descriptions by the same finitely generated $R$-modules: [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] pulls the etale covering back, [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] pulls a constant module sheaf to the constant sheaf of the same module, and the composition compatibility in [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identifies the resulting restriction with $E_j|_T$. Refine the covering objects by affine opens. By [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules] each resulting chart $U_{ja}\to T$ has $E_j|_{U_{ja}}\cong\underline{N_{ja}}$ with $N_{ja}$ finitely generated. Their images are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Quasi-compactness of $T$ therefore selects finitely many charts for each $j$, still jointly surjective. Each chart is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There are finitely many charts in total.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite), applied to the finite affine trivializing charts; local constancy as in sites-modules.tex Tag 093R

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] separately to each of these finitely many affine etale maps $U_{ja}\to T$, and take a common refinement of their finite stratifications. Each chart is now finite etale after restriction. For completeness the common refinement can be reduced and mapped to every original stratum exactly as in step 1; [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] explicitly gives finite etale base change along those maps. Partition each resulting reduced stratum into its finitely many open connected components using [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open], and discard empty strata. Write $S$ for one of these nonempty connected reduced strata. All $W_{ja}=U_{ja}\times_T S\to S$ are finite etale, and for each $j$ the family $(W_{ja})_a$ still covers $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. The number of resulting strata of $X$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (lemma-etale-stratified-finite); topology.tex Tags 04MF and 04ME for connected components

proof.text: Let $W=\coprod_{j,a}W_{ja}$ over $S$. The scheme coproduct and its clopen summands are given by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. This finite coproduct is finite etale: over an affine open of $S$ its ring is the finite product of the finite algebras for its summands, hence finite as a module; etaleness is checked on the disjoint open summands. By [thm-galois-lc-etale], the sheaf $h_W$ represented by $W$ is a finite locally constant sheaf of sets, compatibly with base change and geometric fibres. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-monodromy-torsor] to this sheaf on the nonempty connected $S$. It gives a connected finite etale torsor $c:V\to S$ for a finite group, on which $c^{-1}h_W$ is constant. By the base-change compatibility of the equivalence, this is the sheaf represented by $W\times_S V$. Choose a geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$. The finite group acts on $V$ by $S$-automorphisms, transitively on $V_{\bar s}$ by the torsor condition, so $\operatorname{Aut}_S(V)$ acts transitively. Since $V$ is a connected scheme, it is a connected object of the Galois category $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(S)$ [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object, lem-fet-galois-category], so $g\mapsto g(p)$ is injective on $\operatorname{Aut}_S(V)$ for each $p\in V_{\bar s}$ by part 6 of [lem-galois-axioms]. Hence $\operatorname{Aut}_S(V)$ acts simply transitively and $c$ is a connected Galois cover in [def-galois-object].

source.place: Section Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois), finite monodromy; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 0DV5 and 0DV6

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $v$ of $V$. For each $j$, the covering property supplies a point of some $W_{ja}$ in the geometric fibre over $c(v)$. In a constant finite set sheaf every element of its geometric fibre is the value of a global constant section. Thus the chosen point of $(W\times_S V)_v$ extends to a section of its represented sheaf, that is, a $V$-morphism $s_j:V\to W\times_S V$ over $V$. The inverse images under $s_j$ of the summands $W_{kb}\times_S V$ form a finite clopen partition of $V$. Because $V$ is connected and the selected fibre point belongs to the $(j,a)$ summand, that summand has inverse image all of $V$. Consequently $s_j$ factors through $W_{ja}\times_S V$, giving a map $t_j:V\to U_{ja}$ over $T$. This uses only the definition of a constant sheaf and connectedness, with the clopen summands and fibre compatibility stated by the cited nodes.

source.place: Section Tag 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois), splitting a finite etale object on its monodromy torsor; elementary choice of one sheet through a fibre point

proof.text: Pull the isomorphism $E_j|_{U_{ja}}\cong\underline{N_{ja}}_{U_{ja}}$ back along $t_j$. Constant-module pullback [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] and the composition compatibility of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] give $c^{-1}(E_j|_S)\cong\underline{N_{ja}}_V$. Set $M_{Sj}=N_{ja}$. It is finitely generated over the original coefficient ring $R$, so [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation] makes it finitely presented. Carry out this construction for every $S$ of the finite partition. The same $c$ works for all $j$ because it was chosen for the union of all charts. No statement about finite underlying sets of the modules, or their flatness, was used.

source.place: Tag 093R (lemma-pullback-locally-constant), constant coefficient pullback; algebra.tex Tag 0517 for finite presentation over a Noetherian ring

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, take the empty stratification; there are no cover or module choices to make. If $m=0$ and $X\ne\varnothing$, take the reduction of $X$ and its finitely many nonempty open connected components, using [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and [lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open]. The identity of each component is a connected finite etale Galois cover: its automorphism group and every geometric fibre are singletons. The required module assertions are vacuous. This also treats the zero ring and zero sheaves without an extra restriction.

source.place: Tags 04MF (lemma-locally-Noetherian-locally-connected) and 04ME (lemma-locally-connected); empty-family and empty-space cases
